section_summary: The section begins with Japanese legislative texts concerning trade corporations and national property. It then records Prime Ministers Katayama’s and Ashida’s 1948 addresses to the Diet, together with U.S. diplomatic summaries and press reactions. The final pages concern government reorganization bills and the record of the Second National Diet.

subfiles.title: Trade Corporation Bill, concluding provisions
subfiles.about: Concluding articles regulate trade corporations, ministerial supervision, penalties, establishment, and dissolution.
subfiles.summary: These pages continue a Japanese bill on trade corporations, covering inspection and ministerial orders, use of facilities, penalties for violations, and supplementary provisions. They address establishment procedures, capital payments, dissolution, and related amendments.

subfiles.title: Trade Corporation Bill
subfiles.about: A further text sets out the organization, finances, operations, and supervision of four trade corporations.
subfiles.summary: The bill establishes corporations for raw materials, food, textiles, and manufactured goods, with government capital and prescribed articles of association. It sets out export and import duties, accounting rules, supervision, access to facilities, penalties, and transitional arrangements. Several later pages repeat concluding provisions visible in the preceding document.

subfiles.title: Bill to amend the National Property Law
subfiles.about: Proposed amendments revise the management, disposal, and reporting of national property.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese bill reallocates duties among the Ministry of Finance, other ministries, the Cabinet, and the Board of Audit. It addresses use, transfer, lending, reporting, and review of national property, and provides for a council to prepare further legislation. The closing page states the bill’s constitutional and administrative rationale.

subfiles.title: Bill to amend the National Property Law, further copy
subfiles.about: A further copy presents amendments on national property management and disposal.
subfiles.summary: This copy again sets out amendments concerning the custody, lending, disposal, and accounting of national property. Its supplementary provisions address implementation and the proposed legal study council; the final page gives the reason for the bill.

subfiles.title: Administrative Address of Prime Minister Katayama to Second Session of Diet
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards Katayama’s address and a Government Section bulletin, summarizing the reconstruction program.
subfiles.summary: Katayama proposes production growth, fiscal restraint, food delivery reform, worker rations, administrative and educational changes, repatriation, and preparation for peace.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister Asks Efforts for Expansion of Production to Combat Inflation Scourge
subfiles.about: The clipping prints Katayama’s administrative address on production, inflation, livelihoods, and democratic reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Katayama sets a roughly 40 percent production growth goal and calls for higher food output. He proposes budget restraint, tax enforcement, controlled lending, better worker rations, administrative reform, education and housing measures, repatriation, election reform, and readiness for a peace conference.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister Katayama Outlines Ambitious Program for 1948
subfiles.about: A bulletin summarizes Katayama’s address and lists Diet party strengths.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin highlights production, tax, rationing, labor, administrative, education, election, and peace policies. It also announces interpellations and tabulates party affiliations in both Diet houses.

subfiles.title: Last Minute Changes in Prime Minister’s Address
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sebald reports two changes between Katayama’s delivered address and its advance press text.
subfiles.summary: The delivered speech emphasized signs of recovery and added flood relief measures. It omitted the published reference to the Livelihood Protection Law.

subfiles.title: Summary of Address of Prime Minister Before Diet
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sebald forwards Ashida’s address and newspaper editorials, summarizing policy and criticism.
subfiles.summary: Ashida advocates political cooperation, a middle course, production growth, Allied aid, and preparation for peace. Sebald reports criticism that the address lacked concrete economic and labor measures.

subfiles.title: Prime Minister’s Speech
subfiles.about: The Nippon Times prints Ashida’s March 20 administrative speech.
subfiles.summary: Ashida urges national cooperation and a middle course grounded in peace, liberty, and justice. He discusses inflation, labor and management, industrial technology, agriculture, imports, local government, education, relief, housing, and Japan’s place in a peaceful international order.

subfiles.title: The Prime Minister’s Policy Address
subfiles.about: An editorial criticizes Ashida’s address for omitting concrete measures, especially on labor.
subfiles.summary: The editorial questions Ashida’s labor policy, proposed removal of controls, reliance on foreign capital, and neglect of Japan’s own political instability.

subfiles.title: Editorial Comments of Various Papers on Prime Minister Ashida’s Administrative Speech
subfiles.from: Mainichi, Tokyo Shimbun, Yomiuri, Asahi, Nippon Keizai, and Jiji; translated by Y. Kamii
subfiles.about: Translations collect six newspapers’ reactions to Ashida’s address.
subfiles.summary: The editorials largely find the speech abstract and demand concrete action on labor disputes, wages, inflation, budgets, and production. Some question Ashida’s reliance on foreign assistance or the consistency of his economic views with the coalition agreement. Several reserve judgment until the Cabinet’s policies are carried out.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of Government Reorganization Bills
subfiles.about: The airgram reports the Diet’s consent to withdraw nineteen government reorganization bills.
subfiles.summary: The bills are to be redrafted to specify ministry structures before the planned January 1949 reorganization. Other agency and urgent health or agricultural bills remain under consideration.

subfiles.title: Release of Education Story
subfiles.about: Sebald authorizes release of an education story previously transmitted to several posts.
subfiles.summary: The previously transmitted education story may be released on July 3.

subfiles.title: Public Comments on Accomplishments of the Second National Diet
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch opens a review of legislation and public reaction to the Second National Diet.
subfiles.summary: The opening page lists major enacted and failed bills, MacArthur’s praise, and newspapers’ generally unfavorable assessments.
